  COVID- 19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

  Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed only to observe and address the City Council Meeting of January 4, 2022, at 2:00 p.m. (Or 1:00 p.m. if Closed Session) by telephone, video and other electronic means, as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, City Clerk staff will check and print emails prior to arriving in the Council Chambers. In the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310 -412 - 5280 with any questions.

Inglewood, California
  January 4, 2022

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  January 4, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority into session at the hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority  Members  Padilla,  Morales, and
  Mayor/Chairman Butts; and
  Absent:  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members Dotson, and Faulk.
  City officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  PUBLIC COMMENTS. Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the
  City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item other than the public
  hearing.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  December 22, 2021, in the amount of $809,564.05, and dated December 17, 2021, in the
  amount of $7,969,992.24, are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers
  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Padilla, Morales, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, and Faulk.

301  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – ORDINANCE NO. 22-04 INTRODUCED
  –DESIGNATING CERTAIN PORTIONS OF THE CITY AS AN “EVENT ZONE”
  TO REGULATE CERTAIN ACTIVITIES IN CONNECTION WITH SUPER
  BOWL LVI AND RELATED EVENTS. The City Clerk announced that the next
  scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider an ordinance designating certain
  portions of the City as an “Event Zone” in order to regulate certain activities in
  connection with Super Bowl LVI and related events, that notice was given in the time,
  form and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and communications were
  received, and distributed to the Mayor and City Council Members.

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Louis Atwell, Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director presented the Staff Report
  dated January 4, 2022.
 January 4, 2022

  Christopher Jackson, Sr., Economic and Community Development Director, gave a brief
  presentation.
  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comments portion at the hour of 2:06 p.m.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member Padilla that the City Council does hereby Affirm the Categorical
  Exemption. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Members Dotson, and Faulk.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None; and
  Absent: Council Members Dotson, and Faulk.

  Furthermore, Ordinance No. 22-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  DESIGNATING CERTAIN PORTIONS OF THE CITY AS AN “EVENT
  ZONE” IN ORDER TO REGULATE CERTAIN ACTIVITIES IN
  CONNECTION WITH SUPER BOWL LVI AND RELATED EVENTS

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. The City Manager, Artie Fields, wished everyone a
  Happy New Year. He informed residents that because of the rise of COVID-19, Omicron
  variant, City Hall was taking additional precautions to keep city employees, visitors, and
  the community safe. Effective Wednesday, January 5, 2022, all on-site payments for
  utilities, business taxes, and parking tickets will no longer be accepted at the walk-up
  window. Payments can be made by mail-in or by dropping them in the drop-box outside
  the building. He also provided a telephone number for residents who wished to make
  utility payments by telephone. Finally, he stated anyone who visits City Hall for
  approved appointments must show proof of vaccination, card or electronic, and a picture
  identification for access to the building.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, wished everyone a
  Happy New Year.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported public comments received via email and
  passed out to the Mayor and City Council.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:10 p.m.

  Approved this 8th day of February, 2022.
